conviction_note: The quarter's large book-value drop is already visible through two peers' preliminary Q3 numbers released Oct 14 (ORC -16.6%, IVR -16.1% from June to September) and through DX's own price (down about 18.6% since the July print, now about 1.0x an estimated Sept 30 BV of roughly 10.8-11.2). What is left is small and points both ways: Treasuries rallied about 20bp in October, the company raised capital to deploy into wide spreads, the insider bought a small amount, and the dividend is not covered by Q2 EAD. Findings sum to 0.0, p_up 52, abs_move 1.8, so the scaled number is +0.07. Both measurements are near zero and they agree.
bar: The name trades on book value per share, and there is no sourced consensus for Q3 BV. My own estimate is Sept 30 BV of about $10.8-11.2, from Q2 BV $12.90 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000074/a2q26earningsrelease.htm) with peer Q3 drops applied: ORC 8-K Oct 14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001518621/000143774926032635/ex_1025559.htm), IVR 8-K Oct 14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000076/ivr10142026-8kxex991.htm). The single-source EPS consensus is $0.53 non-GAAP per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DX/earnings-forecasts, Oct 9), against Q2 EAD of $0.36. DX has 'missed' this consensus four quarters running with small moves, so it is not the bar the stock trades on. Price targets were cut Oct 6-7 to $12.50 (KBW) and $12 (BTIG) (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dx.prd/). The bar is unsourced, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest: about 10.4M shares, 4.2% of float, 1.6 days to cover per equibles on the ~2026-08-21 snapshot (https://equibles.com/stocks/dx/shortinterest). This is not FINRA-verified, the Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503, and I found no October settlement. It is not a crowded short. Skew: there is no usable chain (ATM spread 145% of mid, skew null). The front-month put/call OI ratio is 1.09 on only 1,866 contracts, so options give no directional statement. Run-up: -9.85% over 20 days and +1.1% over 5 days. The stock did not fall further on the Oct 14 ORC and IVR pre-releases.

findings.finding: Two agency-mREIT peers pre-announced Q3 2026 on Oct 14, after DX last spoke (Jul 20). Orchid Island: estimated BV $6.02 at Sept 30 against $7.22 at June 30 (-16.6%), total return on equity -12.5%. Invesco Mortgage Capital: estimated BV $6.74 at Sept 30 against $8.03 at June 30 (-16.1%), of which -12.9% came in September alone ($7.74 at Aug 31). Applied to DX's $12.90 June BV at a similar ~8x leverage (8.1x incl. TBAs at Q2), that implies a Sept 30 BV of about $10.8-11.2. Spot $10.98 already trades at about 1.0x that estimate, so the hit looks largely priced. The residual risk is DX landing at the bad end, having added leverage in July (10M ATM shares) just before the widening.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q1 2026, BV fell 6.3% ($13.45 to $12.60), in line with peers (IVR -7.3%, ORC -6.1%, AGNC TBV -5.6%), and the stock moved +0.81% (2026-04-20). On Q2 2026, BV rose 2.4% and the stock moved -1.58% (2026-07-20). BV surprises in line with peers have produced sub-2% moves on all 7 prints in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. DX is down about 18.6% since the July print against an implied BV drop of about 14-16%, and it fell no further on the Oct 14 peer releases (5-day run-up +1.1%). If the market had not absorbed the peer numbers, DX would still trade near 0.85x the June BV with no post-Oct-14 drift. Instead it sits at about 1.0x the peer-implied BV. The unpriced part is only DX's relative outcome against peers, which is unknown.
findings.independence: ORC 8-K Oct 14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001518621/000143774926032635/ex_1025559.htm, via https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Orchid+Island+Capital+Estimates+%240.90+Third-Quarter+GAAP+Loss+Per+Share) and a market series: Agency MBS -3.3% total, -1.0% vs Treasuries in September (https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/3-year-lows-3-year-highs-nine-months-mortgage-rates-surge-749-bond-rout-hits-main-street, ~2026-10-07); Bloomberg MBS index July -1.42% total, -0.44% excess, OAS +7bp (https://insuranceaum.com/agency-mortgage-backed-securities-mbs-market-july-2026, 2026-08-25). The peer, market-series and price evidence all point the same way and describe one fact, so they are merged into this one finding.

findings.finding: Fourth-quarter-to-date rates have reversed part of the September rout. The 10-year closed near 5.29% on Sept 30 (MND recap), peaked around 5.34% in early October, and was about 5.06-5.09% on Oct 15 after its biggest one-day rally in over a year. Freddie/MND 30-year mortgage rates fell from 7.49% (Oct 2) to 7.38% (Oct 14). If DX gives a quarter-to-date BV comment on the 10:00 call, it is more likely flat-to-up than down. However, MBS lagged Treasuries on Sept 30 and again on the Oct 15 rally day (UMBS 6.0 slightly down while the 10-year rallied), so the spread leg is not confirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced record of a DX quarter-to-date BV comment moving the stock. Every print in the baseline moved less than 1.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The rates rally is public and priced in Treasuries. What is not visible is how much of it reached DX's hedged book, given swap and futures hedges and MBS lagging. If the market had priced a QTD BV recovery, DX would have bounced more than +1.1% over 5 days off a level near 1.0x the estimated Sept BV.
findings.independence: Mortgage rates 7.38% on Oct 14, down 6bp on the week (https://themortgagereports.com/mortgage-rates-now/mortgage-rates-today-october-15-2026). Against it: MBS lagged Treasuries on Sept 30 and Oct 15 (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/markets/mbs-recap-09302026, https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/markets/mbs-morning-10152026). This is a proxy; the company has said nothing about Q4.

findings.finding: DX kept raising capital through the widening and deployed it into Agency MBS. It sold about 10M common shares between June 30 and July 24 (237.41M to 247.43M on the 10-Q cover), when the stock traded above the $12.90 BV, which is accretive. It then priced $120M of 9.375% Series D cumulative preferred on Sept 22 (closing Sept 29; ~$115.9M net, overallotment up to 720k more shares), explicitly to buy Agency and other securities. The preferred is non-dilutive to common BV and funds purchases at current-coupon spreads of about 120bp (BofA), which supports forward EAD and the case for an offensive posture on the call. The cost is a high fixed charge ahead of common.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: $391M raised and deployed, BV +2.4%, stock -1.58% on the print. Capital deployment has not been paid for on the print day.
findings.why_not_priced: The offering is public, but its EAD effect (new MBS at wide spreads against a 9.375% preferred coupon) will only show in Q3/Q4 EAD and in management's commentary on return on new capital. If it were priced as distress, the stock would have broken below the estimated BV after Sept 22. It traded ~$11.18 on Sept 25 and ~$10.98 now.
findings.independence: Share count from the 10-Q cover (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667526000078/dx-20260630.htm, filed 2026-07-27); July 2026 ATM supplement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000084/july2026atmprospectus.htm). These are separate documents but the same company's capital decisions.

findings.finding: The Chief Investment Officer, Terrence Connelly, bought 2,500 DX common shares in the open market at $11.18 on 2026-09-25 (Form 4, code P), about $28k, raising his direct holding to 58,695 shares. It is small but sits right after the September BV drawdown. The co-CEO's Sept 8 Form 4 is a tax withholding (code F, 19,528 shares at $12.89), not a sale.
findings.why_not_priced: It is too small to move anything by itself. It is filed because the person who runs the portfolio bought after seeing the quarter-end marks were near, which weakly argues that DX's Q3 is not worse than peers.
findings.independence: Popenoe Form 4, Sept 8 (code F) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000088/wk-form4_1789075318.xml). Same filer stream, different document.

findings.finding: Dividend coverage. Q2 2026 EAD was $0.36 per share against $0.51 of quarterly dividends ($0.17 monthly). The October $0.17 was declared on Oct 12, so management has not signalled a cut. Funding costs moved up in Q3: IVR's repo rate was 3.97% at Sept 30, and a ZeroHedge timeline notes a September Fed hike. A call discussion of EAD under-earning the dividend is a modest negative risk. A cut inside the window is unlikely given the Oct 12 declaration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EAD has 'missed' the $0.50-ish consensus on each of the last four prints (Benzinga) and the moves stayed under 1.8%, so the market has looked through EAD coverage before.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the yield at $10.98 is about 18.6%, which implies some cut risk. If a cut were fully priced, the stock would trade at a discount to estimated BV. It trades at about par.
findings.independence: Q2 EAD $0.36 and dividend $0.51 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000074/a2q26earningsrelease.htm); IVR repo 3.97% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000076/ivr10142026-8kxex991.htm). Cuts against: the Oct 12 declaration held at $0.17.

findings.finding: Sell-side cut price targets before the print but after September: KBW to $12.50 from $15 (Outperform, ~Oct 7) and BTIG to $12 from $14.50 (Buy, ~Oct 6). Both predate the Oct 14 peer pre-releases, so street BV estimates may still be slightly stale against the -16% peer prints. Both ratings stayed Buy, about 9-14% above spot.
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts are in the wire and priced. They are filed so the judges can see where the street bar sits; the snippets do not give the BV estimates behind the targets.

outside_window.finding: AGNC reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-10-19, with its call on Oct 20. Its tangible BV print is the largest peer read-through but lands after DX's exit close.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew. The -9.85% 20-day run-up agrees with the peer-implied BV hit, and the stock now sits at about 1.0x estimated BV, so the evidence is consistent with the drawdown already being in the price rather than cutting against it.
lessons_applied: Rule 'what has worked: a peer's print landing after the company last spoke': the ORC/IVR Oct 14 pre-release finding moved from -0.2 to -0.3, because the Oct 6-7 street targets predate it.
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the Q4-to-date rates finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because its own text says MBS lagged Treasuries on the rally days.
Rules 1 and 6 (reaction history; bar unsourced): kept every finding capped small and kept abs_move near the name's realised daily range rather than raising it; p_up moved from 53 to 52.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): already applied in the draft. The Series D and ATM proceeds were asked what they buy (Agency MBS at wide spreads) and signed positive; unchanged.
Rule 7 (short interest before negatives): checked, 4.2% of float and 1.6 days to cover; no change.
